title: AI-generated worlds are no longer just visuals: Amap ABot-World0.5 supports real-time interaction and audio generation

content_html:
Amap, part of Alibaba Group, has officially released a new-generation general-purpose interactive world model, ABot-World0.5. The update focuses on upgrading realistic physical feedback, synchronized audio-video generation, and real-time reshaping with natural language, and adds interactive skills such as attacking, jumping, and driving. The model ranked first in both physics and overall score on WBench, an authoritative world model benchmark, and is now open for users to try.

This upgrade relies on Phys AI Data, Amap's proprietary data pipeline. Using massive amounts of real-world data, the model learns the dynamic evolution of people, objects, and environments, and further understands the causal relationship between actions and physical feedback. In physics simulation, ABot-World0.5 can simulate rigid-body collisions, soft-body deformation, and motion inertia, generating force outcomes and motion trajectories in real time based on user input.

In multimodal generation, the new model integrates native audio inference into the world generation process, and can generate character footsteps, vehicle engine sounds, object collision sounds, and ambient nature sounds in sync. In interactive control, users can use natural-language commands to adjust the storyline, weather and environment, and character skills in real time, enabling dynamic intervention in the generated world.

In terms of applications, ABot-World0.5 is expected to expand into fields such as embodied AI, film and television production, and game development. Amap's head of R&D said that scaling data is an important foundation for improving world model capabilities, and that real-world data accumulation and systematic data pipelines will continue to drive the model's understanding of complex physical laws.

Currently, ABot-World0.5 is available in two versions: Iris and Halo. Iris supports local deployment and can run on consumer-grade GPUs; Halo uses cloud computing power to deliver higher performance, and users can make API calls or try it online through Reactor, a generative video developer platform.
